title: A personalized comparison
hook: Would a letter using your own drug costs change your plan search?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Contrast generic plan information with a personalized alternative comparison.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Contrast generic plan information with a personalized alternative comparison.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Your toy basket needs one unit of X and four of Y. Plan A charges €10 for X and €30 for Y. What is your bill? Toy inputs A=[1, 4, 10, 30]; B=[1, 4, 20, 10].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[130, 10, 120], [60, 20, 40]]. Labels: Your bill €, X cost €, Y cost €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: A personalized comparison multiplies each price by the quantities this basket needs. A plan with one cheaper item can still cost more overall. The displayed basket explains the total without claiming everyone should choose the same plan.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Drug X units=1, Drug Y units=4, X €/unit=20, Y €/unit=10. What is Your bill €? Answer: 60.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Drug X units=1, Drug Y units=4, X €/unit=20, Y €/unit=10. What is Your bill €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 60. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Personalized letters comparing Medicare drug plans led 28% to switch versus 17% of controls (Kling et al., 2012).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Contrast generic plan information with a personalized alternative comparison.
